origin.name: no earlier file
origin.note: created by Tahoe's kmutil in the kc-hook, in a second kmutil run, after the boot collection and its member list exist

args.tool_note: copied to builder scratch and re-signed ad hoc; it runs only while linking
args.builder_note: on an Intel host only (uname -m x86_64: a hao image, Golden Gate's Recovery): kmutil links in the running system's libKernelCollectionBuilder, which there is Golden Gate's and refuses x86_64, so src/kmutil_builder.py makes the copy a thin x86_64 kmutil that loads Tahoe's from the row; in the builder VM (arm64) it loads the running system's, as before
args.build_directory_note: inside the System volume while linking and removed after; its path is linked into the BootKC, so changing it changes the bytes hao-opencore's repairs are bound to
args.kexts: the image's Intel driver tree: Tahoe Extensions, KDK kexts, OCLP's hardware kexts, found by kmutil under the root
args.name: sys
args.boot_collection: BootKernelExtensions.kc (-B, as for the boot collection)
args.elide_identifiers: every identifier in System/Library/KernelCollections/BootKernelExtensions.kc.elides (--elide-identifier), so no driver is in both collections

edits.reason: the rest of the Intel drivers load from a system collection that repeats nothing the boot collection already holds
